summary: Utah State hosts Washington State tonight. Monday’s quarterback update left the starter unresolved; watch the final choice, keep Wood involved beyond the opening drive and make the Cougars sustain their possessions.

items.headline: Monday’s update left Utah State’s Friday quarterback choice unresolved
items.tldr: Mendenhall declined to name the starter after both quarterbacks played at Boise State. Follow tonight’s final choice, then watch whether the offense can maintain its timing.

items.headline: Local analysis calls for steadier involvement from Eli Wood
items.tldr: Cache Valley Daily traced how Wood’s targets disappeared between productive drives at Boise State. Watch whether the passing game keeps finding him when the first series is over.

items.headline: Jacobs rushed for 139 yards at Boise State
items.tldr: His first 100-yard rushing game gives the offense something to build on. Watch the blocks that create space and whether Utah State can turn a long gain into a finished drive.

items.headline: Washington State scored only on two field goals against Fresno State
items.tldr: The Cougars lost 26-6 and went scoreless after halftime. Utah State should make them sustain a drive, with sound coverage and tackles instead of a quick explosive play.

items.headline: Tonight’s home game starts at 7 p.m. MT on The CW
items.tldr: Maverik Stadium gates open at 5:30 p.m. MT, and fans are asked to wear blue. Set the arrival or broadcast reminder for tonight.

lead.headline: Keep Wood in the next series.
lead.body: Watch the passing game return to Wood after the opening script. Pair those throws with running lanes for Jacobs, then make Washington State earn its response after a score.

matchup.question: What should Utah State emphasize on Friday?
matchup.answer: Follow the quarterback choice without assuming a split. Watch whether the next series keeps Wood involved and gives Jacobs room; on defense, finish the tackle before a short completion becomes an easy answer.
